sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Sterling Heights?
sections.html:
Sterling Heights splits the work between two city offices and one county office. The Office of Treasury, at 40555 Utica Road, bills and collects current-year tax and is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The Assessing Office sets values and processes ownership changes. Macomb County takes over bills that reach March 1 unpaid.

The city asks owners to report changes to the right desk. A new mortgage company is a call to Treasury at 586-446-2780. A transfer of ownership or a change in principal residence information goes to Assessing at 586-446-2340. If an escrow account pays your tax, the original bill goes to the escrow agent and you receive a clearly marked courtesy copy.

Every property in the city gets two bills a year, both from the City Treasurer's Office.

sections.h2: When are Sterling Heights summer and winter taxes due?
sections.html:
The summer bill is payable from July 1 through the first business day in September, and the winter bill from December 1 through the end of February, both without penalty. The city mails summer bills in late June and winter bills in late November.

Sterling Heights tax bill schedule and late charges, from the city's Property Tax Information page
BillMailedPayable without penaltyIf left unpaid
SummerLate JuneJuly 1 through the first business day in SeptemberOne-half of 1% per month after September 1 through the end of February
WinterLate NovemberDecember 1 through the end of FebruaryOn March 1, an added 3% interest, then transfer to Macomb County

The March 1 step applies to any balance left on either bill. After that date, and for any bill from a prior year, payment goes to the Macomb County Building at 1 South Main in Mount Clemens, phone 586-469-5190, where more penalties are added.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Sterling Heights tax bill?
sections.html:
The city offers a return envelope, drop boxes, a card line and an eCheck option. Which one fits depends on how close the deadline is.

  • Mail the check, payable to City of Sterling Heights, to PO Box 88528, Chicago, IL 60680-1528, using the envelope that comes with the bill. Put the parcel ID on the check.
  • Use a secured drop box on the city center campus, along the circular drive near the Police Department entrance or near the Utica entrance to City Hall.
  • Pay by card at 877-495-2729 or on the payment website. Point and Pay charges a convenience fee, and American Express is not accepted.
  • Pay from a checking or savings account through the eCheck option on the same website.

Treasury also moves unpaid water and sewer balances onto the tax roll. The city says delinquent account reports are transferred to the rolls after City Manager approval on a semi-annual basis. A seller with a past-due utility account should settle it before closing so the amount does not show up on a tax bill.

sections.h2: How does Sterling Heights set a home's taxable value, and what changes after a sale?
sections.html:
The Assessing Office calculates assessed value, which is 50% of true cash value, using a two-year sales study. Michigan voters approved Proposal A on March 15, 1994, and it created taxable value, which is the lesser of the state equalized value or a capped value. The cap is last year's taxable value raised by inflation or 5%, whichever is less, plus any construction changes.

A sale lifts that cap. In the year after a transfer, taxable value becomes the state equalized value with no limit on the change, so the seller's bill can sit well below what the new owner is billed. The sale price alone does not set the new value. The Assessing Office adjusts land and building values across the city from sales in the study period and does not reassess a parcel from a single transaction.

Sellers who have owned for many years should tell buyers to expect a higher first bill. The buyer must file a Property Transfer Affidavit (form 2766) with Assessing within 45 days of the transfer.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Sterling Heights assessment or claim the Principal Residence Exemption?
sections.html:
The Assessing Office usually mails the Notice of Assessment, Taxable Valuation, and Property Classification on the last day of February. The March Board of Review typically starts on the third Monday in March, and two three-member committees of city residents hear appeals of assessments, classification and hardship exemptions. Owners who appeal get written notice of the decision no later than the first Monday in June. A residential owner who disagrees can go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

  • Principal Residence Exemption: if the notice shows 0%, file form 2368 with Assessing by June 1 to affect the summer levy or by November 1 to affect the winter levy.
  • Rescission: an owner who stops living in the house must file form 2602 to end the exemption.
  • Tax information lookup: the city posts an online property tax lookup.

sections.h2: What is Sterling Heights like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Sterling Heights is a second-ring suburb about 14 to 20 miles north of downtown Detroit, in Macomb County. It covers roughly 36 square miles of land, and the Clinton River crosses the northeast corner. Until the 1950s it was Sterling Township, farmland known for rhubarb, and it became a city in 1968. The word Heights was added to the name to avoid a clash with the village of Sterling in Arenac County.

Growth came with the auto plants. Chrysler and Ford jobs drew families through the 1960s and 1970s, and Lakeside Mall opened in 1976. Many residents are Chaldean and Assyrian, and the area around 15 Mile Road and Ryan has the nickname Little Nineveh. Two freeways frame the city, M-53 (Van Dyke) and M-59 (Hall Road), with Mound Road running north and south and the mile roads from 14 Mile to 20 Mile crossing east to west.

Two school districts split the city: Utica Community Schools covers the northern half, with Stevenson and Henry Ford II high schools, and Warren Consolidated Schools covers the southern half, with Sterling Heights High School. Winters are cold, with 39.1 days a year when the temperature stays below freezing, which is worth remembering when buyers inspect roofs and basements.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Sterling Heights housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 133,931 residents in Sterling Heights as of July 1, 2025, living in 51,736 households with an average of 2.57 people each. For 2020 to 2024, 75.8% of homes were owner-occupied, the median value was $274,300, and median gross rent was $1,292.

Monthly owner costs run $1,681 with a mortgage and $666 without one. Median household income was $79,909 in 2024 dollars. Ask the Assessing Office for the figures on your own parcel, since a city-wide median says little about one street.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Sterling Heights summer tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: The last day is the first business day in September. After September 1, the city adds one-half of 1% per month through the end of February.

faqs.q: Where does my Sterling Heights tax go if I miss the February deadline?
faqs.a: It goes to Macomb County. On March 1 the city adds 3% interest and transfers any balance on a summer or winter bill, and payment is then made at the Macomb County Building, 1 South Main, Mount Clemens, at 586-469-5190.

faqs.q: Who files the Property Transfer Affidavit after a Sterling Heights sale?
faqs.a: The buyer files it. Form 2766 is due at the Assessing Office within 45 days of the transfer, and blank forms are available at the office and on the city and state Treasury websites.

faqs.q: How do I stop the Principal Residence Exemption after I move out of my Sterling Heights house?
faqs.a: File a Request to Rescind Homeowner's Principal Residence Exemption (form 2602) with the Assessing Office. A buyer who will live there files form 2368 by June 1 for the summer levy or November 1 for the winter levy.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sterling Heights property tax by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. Call 877-495-2729 to pay by card, and expect a convenience fee from Point and Pay. American Express is not accepted. The payment website also takes eCheck payments from a checking or savings account.
